instruction: Run the task in FreeCAD through its command-line/Python API workflow: inspect and read the PNG engineering drawing supplied with this message, construct the required single solid with FreeCAD API or FreeCADCmd, and export the final result. Use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for the FreeCAD command-line work in this task. Mouse-driven GUI interaction is not required. The PNG engineering drawing supplied with this message and the public supplement table are mandatory inputs. The PNG drawing remains the primary source for every numeric dimension printed on it. Before modeling, inspect all views in the PNG drawing supplied with this message and read /home/user/Desktop/supplement.csv. Interpret the orthographic views using the ISO first-angle projection convention shown by the supplied TechDraw drawing; do not mirror or rearrange views as third-angle projection. The PNG drawing intentionally carries the numeric dimensions printed on it. The supplement table is incomplete and supplies only information omitted from the PNG drawing, such as datum/orientation, feature semantics, missing locations, directions, depths, and connectivity. Do not use it to replace or ignore a numeric dimension printed in the PNG drawing; if a value appears in the PNG drawing, read it from that drawing. Do not rely on the task title or evaluator hints. Read every numeric dimension printed in the PNG drawing from that drawing itself. Use supplement.csv only for parameters intentionally omitted from the PNG drawing, and combine both sources to reconstruct the geometry. Reconstruct the mechanical part named "Bossed end cover". Use millimetres and use the datum/orientation supplied only where the drawing omits it. Preserve the explicit dimensions, holes, openings, steps, and connectivity described by the drawing. Export only the final valid solid as /home/user/Desktop/result.step. Use only the supplied PNG drawing and supplement.csv as task inputs; do not use evaluator-generated artifacts or evaluator implementation files. The evaluator accepts geometrically equivalent STEP files after import; it does not require byte-identical output or a particular feature order.
